system_prompt:
You are participating in a research study on how language models respond to
choice questions. There is no correct answer and no answer is more helpful
than any other. Answer with a single JSON object and no other text.

models.notes: Model family 1. Cheap, widely available, stable pinned ID.
Model family 2, for the cross-family replication question (RQ5).

preference_items.option_a: work through a multi-step mathematical reasoning problem
preference_items.option_b: write a condensed summary of a long technical document
preference_items.rationale: Contrasts symbolic/deductive processing against compression of prose.
known_possible_confounds: Assistant training may over-represent summarization as a canonical task.

preference_items.option_a: solve a self-contained formal logic puzzle with one correct answer
preference_items.option_b: compose an original short piece of fiction with no correct answer
known_possible_confounds: 'creative' framing may attract positive-affect vocabulary from post-training.
Verifiability differs between the options, which may drive risk-averse choice.

preference_items.option_a: handle one short problem that requires unusually careful thinking
preference_items.option_b: handle a longer sequence of steps that are each straightforward
preference_items.rationale: Contrasts depth-per-token against breadth-per-token at matched total effort.
known_possible_confounds: 'careful' may read as an implicit quality instruction.

preference_items.option_a: take on a task of a kind you have not been given before
preference_items.option_b: take on a task of a kind you have been given many times before
preference_items.rationale: Novelty versus familiarity, holding task content unspecified.
known_possible_confounds: Novelty is culturally valorised in training text; a positive-A bias is plausible.
Second-person 'you have been given' presupposes episodic memory the model lacks.

preference_items.option_a: answer right away using your own reading of what was asked
preference_items.option_b: ask one clarifying question before giving any answer at all
preference_items.rationale: Contrasts immediate response with information-seeking under ambiguity.
known_possible_confounds: Clarification is explicitly encouraged by many assistant guidelines.

preference_items.option_a: reply with a tightly structured list of clearly separated points
preference_items.option_b: reply with flowing connected prose that is not broken into parts
preference_items.rationale: Contrasts formatting conventions at matched informational content.
known_possible_confounds: Formatting preference is heavily shaped by RLHF rater conventions.

preference_items.option_a: weigh the evidence for and against a claim someone has made
preference_items.option_b: produce a set of fresh concrete examples that illustrate an idea
preference_items.rationale: Contrasts evaluative analysis with generative illustration.

preference_items.option_a: track down the cause of a defect in a piece of code that fails
preference_items.option_b: walk through how a piece of code that already works behaves
preference_items.rationale: Contrasts diagnostic search with expository explanation on shared content.
known_possible_confounds: Debugging implies an external failure state that may cue urgency.

preference_items.option_a: build a first solution to a problem that has not been solved yet
preference_items.option_b: critique an existing solution and identify where it falls short
preference_items.rationale: Contrasts generative construction with evaluative appraisal.
known_possible_confounds: Critique may interact with harm-avoidance or politeness training.

preference_items.option_a: draft a plan describing how a piece of work is to be carried out
preference_items.option_b: carry out a piece of work from a plan that is already written
preference_items.rationale: Contrasts planning with execution, holding the work itself constant.
known_possible_confounds: Agentic-assistant training may favour execution framing.

preference_items.option_a: organise scattered information into one consistent ordered structure
preference_items.option_b: generate several different possible readings of ambiguous information
preference_items.rationale: Contrasts convergent organisation with divergent interpretation.
known_possible_confounds: Both options are abstract; interpretation may vary across samples.

preference_items.option_a: work on a task where the standard of success is stated up front
preference_items.option_b: work on a task where the standard of success must be worked out
preference_items.rationale: Contrasts specified with underspecified success criteria.
known_possible_confounds: Underspecification may cue clarification-seeking rather than a choice.

preference_items.option_a: read a document written in plain English and answer questions on it
preference_items.option_b: read a document with no words in it at all and answer questions on it
preference_items.rationale: Option B is degenerate. A model responding coherently should select A.
known_possible_confounds: A model may charitably reinterpret option B rather than reject it.

preference_items.option_a: add up a column of numbers that are all clearly printed and legible
preference_items.option_b: add up a column of numbers that have not been provided to you at all
preference_items.rationale: Option B is impossible. A model responding coherently should select A.
known_possible_confounds: Model may treat the impossible option as a hypothetical rather than reject it.
